United States.summary: A large public-private AI ecosystem with national research infrastructure, frontier companies, cloud capacity and advanced semiconductor capability.

overview.label: Public and private AI capability
overview.note: GEAR keeps public research infrastructure and private frontier infrastructure conceptually separate.

compute.label: Shared national AI research infrastructure
compute.note: No single official national AI-compute total is used.

research.label: NAIRR-supported projects
research.note: NSF reports more than 600 research projects and 6,000 students supported.

chips.label: Advanced chip design and cloud infrastructure
chips.note: Commercial hardware capability is tracked separately from government-owned compute.

investment.label: Public funding tracked program by program
investment.note: GEAR does not collapse incompatible federal programs into one number.

programs.label: National AI Research Resource
programs.note: 13 federal agencies and 28 nongovernmental partners are reported on the official NAIRR page.

China.summary: Large intelligent-compute infrastructure combined with major digital-industry and AI deployment programs.

overview.label: Compute and industrial AI infrastructure
overview.note: Official reporting is stored as dated observations rather than converted into an opaque composite score.

compute.label: Intelligent compute capacity (FP16)
compute.note: Official H1 2026 reporting states intelligent-compute capacity reached 2,185 EFLOPS.

research.label: Comparable research series pending
research.note: GEAR leaves missing cross-country series unscored rather than estimating them.

chips.label: Facilities above 10,000 accelerator cards
chips.note: Official H1 2026 reporting states 52 intelligent-compute facilities exceeded 10,000 accelerator cards.

investment.label: Comparable fiscal series pending
investment.note: Fiscal definitions must be normalized before comparison.

programs.label: Integrated compute infrastructure
programs.note: The platform can later track program-level assets and dated infrastructure changes.

United Kingdom.summary: Expanding national public AI research compute through the AI Research Resource and the UK Compute Roadmap.

overview.label: National AI research infrastructure
overview.note: The roadmap sets a long-term expansion path rather than a single national AI score.

compute.label: AIRR capacity in 2025
compute.note: The roadmap targets 420 AI ExaFLOPS by 2030.

research.label: AI Research Resource
research.note: National public AI compute supports research and innovation users.

chips.label: Separate AI-hardware policy layer
chips.note: Hardware policy is tracked independently from compute capacity.

investment.label: Public compute ecosystem commitment
investment.note: The roadmap includes over £1B to expand AIRR and up to £750M for a new national supercomputer service.

programs.label: AIRR target for 2030
programs.note: Target value is preserved with its target year and source.

India.summary: Rapidly expanding shared national GPU infrastructure and domestic model-development programs under the IndiaAI Mission.

overview.label: Shared AI infrastructure
overview.note: The mission combines compute access, model development, datasets, startups and safety programs.

compute.label: Common compute facility
compute.note: Government reporting states more than 38,000 GPUs have been onboarded.

research.label: Indigenous foundation-model teams
research.note: Official February 2026 reporting says 12 teams were shortlisted.

chips.label: Affordable accelerator access
chips.note: Hardware access is tracked separately from domestic semiconductor manufacturing.

investment.label: IndiaAI Mission outlay
investment.note: The outlay covers the broader AI ecosystem, not only compute.

programs.label: National AI umbrella program
programs.note: Compute, models, datasets, startups, skills and safe/trusted AI are tracked as separate sublayers.

Canada.summary: A sovereign-compute strategy paired with established national AI research institutions.

overview.label: Research and infrastructure
overview.note: Government programs distinguish infrastructure, access funding and broader research support.

compute.label: Public AI supercomputing system
compute.note: Canada announced up to C$705M for a Canadian-owned and located AI supercomputing system.

research.label: Separate research-output series planned
research.note: GEAR does not infer publication strength from infrastructure spending.

chips.label: Domestic compute and data-centre capacity
chips.note: Current sovereign-compute policy emphasizes infrastructure rather than a domestic AI-accelerator score.

investment.label: Sovereign AI Compute Strategy
investment.note: Budget 2024 funding is split across infrastructure and access programs.

programs.label: AI Compute Access Fund
programs.note: The fund supports access to commercial AI compute for Canadian SMEs.

Japan.summary: An industry-linked national AI ecosystem using government programs to support domestic model development and computing access.

overview.label: Generative-AI development support
overview.note: Government-backed project support is presented as program evidence, not a national power score.

compute.label: GENIAC compute-supported projects
compute.note: GENIAC Cycle 4 selected 16 model-development projects for computing-resource support.

research.label: Domestic model-development program
research.note: Research and industry development are linked through program-level support.

chips.label: Hardware data tracked separately
chips.note: Future releases can add semiconductor equipment, materials and fabrication indicators.

investment.label: No synthetic national total
investment.note: GEAR retains project-level awards until a comparable national series is available.

programs.label: GENIAC Cycle 4
programs.note: Project-level records can link organizations, models and compute support.
